rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is intrinsically transcendent and exalted above claims that He has partners or daughters.
rows.anchor: من أن معه آلهة وأن له بنات

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: The verse expresses astonishment at how far the Lord of dominion stands above their claims; ʿuluwwan means taʿāliyan, as in Noah 71:17, and the contrast is absolute being versus impossible nonbeing.
rows.anchor: تنزيه وتعجيب من قولهم أي ما أبعد من له الملك والربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one in essence and attributes; shirk begins in supposition, and believers too may idolize the self, a spouse, or commerce through obedience, love, or reliance.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الله أحد في ذاته وواحد في صفاته

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: He fainted while reciting the Fātiḥa because people profess worship and dependence on God while obeying their own desires and turning to other doors for help.
rows.anchor: حكي أن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله كان إذا قرأ في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should repeatedly renew the pledge of divine unity, which brings forgiveness and advancement among the righteous and near ones.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يكرر ذكر التوحيد ويجدد العهد الذي بينه وبين ذي العرش المجيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He relates that the newly created Throne shook until God taught the testimony of faith; it shook again when its first speaker recited it, then was promised that every servant who says it will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لما خلق الله العرش وهو أعظم مخلوق اضطرب أربعة وعشرين ألف عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ is declaring God free of the defects of possibility and origination; the heavens and earth do so by the signs of their existence, power, and wisdom, while their inhabitants speak praise aloud.
rows.anchor: التسبيح تنزيه الحق وتبعيده عن نقائص الإمكان والحدوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's generality encompasses both spoken praise and the mute signs of createdness that testify to God's transcendence.
rows.anchor: معنى منتظم لما ينطق به لسان المقال ولسان الحال بطريق عموم المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every thing, whether animal or plant, indicates its Maker, power, and wisdom; polytheists fail to understand because their defective reflection does not follow their admission that God created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: من الأشياء حيوانا كان أو نباتا يدل على الصانع وقدرته وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forbearance delays requital despite their heedlessness and associationism, and He forgives those who repent and return to unity.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لم يعاجلكم بالعقوبة مع أنتم عليه من الإعراض عن التدبر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والبيضاوي وأبو السعود
rows.claim: The exoteric commentators explain the failure to understand praise by the polytheists' neglect of sound reflection and their failure to follow their admission of the Creator.
rows.anchor: هذا ما عليه الزمخشري والبيضاوي وأبو السعود ومن يليهم من أهل الظاهر

rows.speaker: علي السمرقندي
rows.claim: He reports that the righteous early Muslims take both occurrences of tasbīḥ literally, and calls this the sounder view: if inanimate speech is possible, its praise should be accepted too.
rows.anchor: ذهب السلف الصالح إلى أن التسبيح في الآية في المحلين محمول على حقيقته وهو الأصح

rows.speaker: أهل الحقيقة
rows.claim: They apply “you do not understand” to Muslims and polytheists alike: hearing sounds is insufficient without reflecting on what the speaker conveys and praising God accordingly.
rows.anchor: عام للمسلمين والمشركين أي : لا تسمعون فلا تفقهون تسبيحهم

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: He says created things praise in languages unlike human languages, though God may let some servants, such as David and Solomon, understand some inanimate beings and animals.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس بلغتكم ويجوز أن يفهم تعالى بعض عباده تسبيح بعض الجمادات والعجماوات كداود وسليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects language difference as a sufficient explanation: some beings have varied, audible sounds while others have no audible sound, yet all are affirmed to praise.
rows.anchor: لأن لغات ماله أصوات مختلفة لا تفقه وإن كانت مسموعة

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
rows.claim: Salmi transmits from him that all created beings praise God in different languages, but only a divinely learned heart with opened inner hearing can hear and understand them.
rows.anchor: سلمى از ابو عثمان مغربي قدس سرهما نقل ميكندكه تمام مكونات باختلاف لغات تسبيح الهي ميكويند

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: He offers two explanations for a stone's speech: God may create life and intelligence with it, or create a sound without life.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون نطق الحجر كلاما مقرونا بحياة وعلم ويحتمل أن يكون صوتا مجردا

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Against those who deny cognition to inanimate things, he says life permeates the world; all things hearing the call to prayer can testify, though God veils this life from humans and jinn except chosen knowers, who directly hear their praise and speech.
rows.anchor: سر الحياة سار في جميع العالم وقد ورد أن كل شيء سمع صوت المؤذن من رطب ويابس يشهد له

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: A mountain crumbled at the manifestation because it knew God's greatness; without that apprehension it would not have crumbled.
rows.anchor: وكذلك اندكاك الجبل لما وقع التجلي إنما كان ذلك منه لمعرفته بعظمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Every particle glorifies God: living beings praise in their own tongues, while inanimate things use a heavenly tongue; their praise thanks Him for bringing them into being and nurturing them, unlike human praise.
rows.anchor: ينزهه عما يقولون من كل نقيصة ذرات المكونات وأجزاء المخلوقات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Each particle has a spiritual kingdom: the afterlife is living rather than inert, so every particle has a spiritual tongue that praises its Maker and thanks Him for His gifts.
rows.anchor: الملكوت باطن الكون وهو الآخرة والآخرة حيوان لا جماد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: This spiritual speech explains the pebbles praising in the Prophet's hand, the earth recounting its news, body parts testifying, and heaven and earth answering God's command.
rows.anchor: وبهذا اللسان نطق الحصى في يد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبهذا تنطق الأرض يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God was forbearing from eternity in bringing into being those who would associate partners with Him, and forgives those who repent of such claims.
rows.anchor: في الأزل إذ أخرج من العدم من يتولد منه أن يتخذ مع الله آلهة أخرى

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Each thing's distinctive property, longing for and preserving what completes it, manifests its uniqueness and implicitly declares God one; its pursuit of perfection denies deficiency, and its display of perfection praises its giver.
rows.anchor: لكل شيء خاصية لا يشاركه فيها غيره وكما لا يخصه دون ما عداه يشتاقه ويطلبه

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: The hidden barrier keeps Quraysh disbelievers in the afterlife from recognizing the Prophet's prophethood and rank; “covered” can mean imperceptible or possessing a covering.
rows.anchor: يحجبهم من أن يدركوك على ما أنت عليه من النبوة

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: He reports that the polytheists harassed the Prophet while he prayed, and that Umm Lahab came with a stone to strike him but slipped; on this reading reciting the Qur'an means praying because prayer includes it.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون يؤذون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مصليا وجاءت أم لهب بحجر لترضخه فزل

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: He suggests revelation concerned Abu Sufyan, al-Naḍr, Abu Jahl, and Umm Jamil, whom God made unable to see the Prophet when they passed as he recited; the author says this overlooks the next verse and its report is problematic.
rows.anchor: لعل الأولى أن يحمل على ما روي أنها أنزلت في أبي سفيان والنضير وأبي جهل وأم جميل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The perfected reciter embodies the Qur'an's character and reaches the highest nearness; traversing luminous and dark veils makes him hidden from those cut off from God.
rows.anchor: استيفاء جميع آي القرآن في الحقيقة هو التخلق بأخلاق القرآن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A transmitted saying equates the Qur'an's verses with Garden ranks: embodying all its verses reaches the highest rank, and the connected one behind the veil is hidden from the disconnected.
rows.anchor: إن عدد آي القرآن على عدد درج الجنة فمن استوفى جميع آي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who takes refuge in God's Book is in a secure fortress; whoever instead relies on knowledge or self is in danger, as the cited verses warn.
rows.anchor: من تحصن بكتابه فهو في حصن حصين والمضيع لوقته من تحصن بعلمه أو بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many coverings of the heart are likened to cases that keep Qur'anic truth from entering; grammatically, “lest they understand” gives the purpose, though its construction is disputed.
rows.anchor: أغطية كثيرة جمع كنان وهو الغطاء

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufan grammatical analysis allows the phrase to mean that God covered their hearts out of aversion to their understanding it; Basran grammarians object that deleting “lā” is rarer than deleting a genitive complement.
rows.anchor: وهو على رأي الكوفيين ولا يرضاه البصريون لقلة حذف لا بالنسبة إلى حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: The heart-covering and deafness are figures for hearts and ears recoiling from and refusing the truth, as though encased or blocked.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لتجافي قلوبهم عن الحق ونبوها عن قبوله واعتقاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejection is real in effect: accumulated inward veils obstruct a heart whose original disposition would support understanding and perception, and the coverings block both the meaning and wording of the miraculous Qur'an.
rows.anchor: تراكم الحجب المعنوية على القلب والفطرة الأصلية وإن كانت مقتضية للفقه والإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “God alone” means that no deity accompanies Him; grammatically, the verbal expression for being one is replaced by a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: إذا قلت لا إله إلا الله وهو مصدر وقع موقع الحال أصله تحده وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase means that the rejecters turned back and fled; نفور is either a verbal noun like sitting or a plural meaning those who flee.
rows.anchor: أعرضوا ورجعوا حال كونهم نافرين والنفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in “they listen by it” marks their manner—mockery, frivolity, and contempt—or alternatively the cause for which they listen.
rows.anchor: من اللغو والاستخفاف والهزؤ بك وبالقرآن فمحل به حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says two men from Abd al-Dar stood on each side while the Prophet recited, clapping, whistling, and interrupting him with poetry.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنه كان يقوم عن يمينه صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ رجلان من عبدالدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clauses intensify the warning: God knows both their taunting manner of listening and their secret conversation; نجوى is a predicate with an omitted “possessors,” and the next clause labels them wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وفائدته تأكيد الوعيد بالاخبار بأنه كما يقع الاستماع المزبور منهم يتعلق به العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their private talk is distinct from the way they listen: they tell one another that anyone following the Prophet would only be following a bewitched man, unjustly replacing messenger with “bewitched.”
rows.anchor: أي : سحر فجن فمن ظلمهم وضعوا اسم المسحور موضع المبعوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents compare the Prophet to a poet, magician, and madman; the commentary also reports the accusation of soothsayer.
rows.anchor: مثلوك بالشاعر والساحر والمجنون

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He specifies the accusations as madman, magician, soothsayer, and poet.
rows.anchor: وترا توصيف كردند بمجنون وساحر وكاهن وشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have lost the path of sound argument and cannot make a persuasive attack; following desire, they consume tales, magic, and poetry, while sound listening would reveal God's words and attributes.
rows.anchor: إلى طعن يمكن أن يقبله أحد فيتهافتون ويخطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of desire in every age prefer tales and worldly gossip, slander, and whisperings to God's speech and the counsel of those who command right and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: إكباب أهل الهوى في كل عصر على استماع القصص والأساطير معرضين عن كلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying in the Torah rebukes the servant who studies a friend's letter carefully while neglecting God's repeatedly explained Book and turning away when God addresses him.
rows.anchor: وأنت في الطريق تمشي فتعدل عن الطريق وتقعد لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan deniers forget their beginning: they were made from earth, indeed from nothing, as Mary 19:9 says; they reject resurrection because decomposed bones seem incompatible with renewed life.
rows.anchor: نسوا بداية خلقهم أنهم خلقوا من تراب بل أنهم خلقوا من لا شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time word is purely adverbial; its governing verb is an implied “we raise” or “we restore,” since the following interrogative construction cannot govern backward.
rows.anchor: قوله إذا متمحضة للظرفية وهو الأظهر والعامل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their specification of the decomposed state heightens the denial, not limits it: they reject revival even if the body remains intact, stressing the state most opposed to life; “new creation” is a cognate-like accusative or a circumstantial description.
rows.anchor: وإن كان البدن على حاله بل لتقوية الإنكار للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is figurative: even if they became stone, iron, or something they consider still less capable of life, God's power can restore them; bodies had life before and accept accidents, so revival is no harder.
rows.anchor: فإنكم مبعوثون ومعادون لا محالة

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: He reads the command to become stone or iron as a challenge and rebuke, not a binding demand.
rows.anchor: هو أمر تعجيز وتوبيخ لا أمر إلزام

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He says the command is metaphorical contempt rather than a literal request; “what is greater in your breasts” can mean the heavens and mountains.
rows.anchor: ليس الأمر ههنا على حقيقته بل على المجاز لأن المقصود إهانتهم وقلة المبالاة بهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most interpreters take the greatest thing in their minds to be death itself: even if they were death, God would bring them back to life.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه الموت إذ ليس في النفس شيء أكبر من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question of who can restore them forgets their origin; the one who first created them from nothing can restore them, and they shake their heads in disbelief before mocking the timing of resurrection.
rows.anchor: من غير مثال وكنتم ترابا ما شم رائحة الحياة

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Resurrection is near because every future event is near, or because most of time has already passed; in God's usage ʿasā conveys certainty, so judgment and punishment are near.
rows.anchor: هو قريب لأن عسى في الأصل للطمع والإشفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls people from their graves as He called them from nonexistence; their rising and response are described as a call and answer to show how easily it occurs.
rows.anchor: من الأجداث كما دعاكم من العدم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: He takes the call literally as the audible final trumpet blast, like the caller in Qāf 50:41, and response as compliance; al-Kashifi identifies the caller as Israfil.
rows.anchor: يدعوكم بالنداء الذي يسمعكم وهو النفخة الأخيرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the call's purpose is to bring people before God for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: المقصود منها الإحضار للمحاسبة والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although calls also summon people to gathering and to their books, the context is resurrection, so this means the initial call to rise and be raised.
rows.anchor: والمراد في هذا المقام هو الدعوة الأولى لأن الكلام في البعث

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says the resurrected brush dust from their heads and praise and sanctify God for His power to resurrect, though that praise then brings no benefit.
rows.anchor: كما قال سعيد بن جبير أنهم ينفضون التراب عن رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: He interprets “with His praise” as by God's will and command, comparing the command to glorify in Qāf 50:39.
rows.anchor: بإرادته وأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the terrifying resurrection people think they stayed only briefly, whether in graves or the world; worldly life seems long to those with hopes, but terror erases their awareness of its duration, so the wise should spend the fleeting life on the lasting one.
rows.anchor: بالنسبة إلى لبثكم بعد الإحياء إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should address polytheists with the best words, without harshness, following the instruction about disputing with the People of the Book; the verb form is imperative in sense with its n deleted.
rows.anchor: للمشركين عند محاورتهم معهم بني على حذف النون لما كان بمعنى الأمر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Divine favor toward those called His servants yields the best speech, deeds, and character: sincere invitation to unity, action in the law and spiritual path toward reality, and kindness, patience, forgiveness, and gentle counsel toward people.
rows.anchor: اختصاص بعض العباد بتشريف الإضافة إلى نفسه يؤدي إلى تأثير نظر العناية فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan stirs quarrels and corrupts relations, so harsh speech may provoke stubbornness and more disorder.
rows.anchor: أي : يفسد ويهيج الشر والمراء بينهم فلعل المخاشنة بهم تفضي إلى العناد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Wise people in every age should counsel their contemporaries as the Companions did, treating them as they would have done in the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: فينبغي لعقلاء كل زمان أن يكونوا في باب النصيحة مثل الأصحاب رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's enmity is manifest and longstanding: he seeks human ruin, as shown by his expulsion of Adam from the Garden and removal of his garment of light.
rows.anchor: وقد أبان عداوته لهم إذ أخرج أباهم من الجنة ونزع عنه لباس النور

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف والبيضاوي وأبو السعود
rows.claim: They take this as the best reply believers should give: God may guide disbelievers to faith or let them die in unbelief, so believers must not declare them damned when their end is unknown.
rows.anchor: فهو تفسير للتي هي أحسن وما بينهما اعتراض أي : قولوا لهم هذه الكلمة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The best reply means courteous conversation; mercy is rescue from Meccan persecution and punishment is the Meccans being given power over believers, so the address is to the faithful.
rows.anchor: المراد بالتي هي أحسن هي المحاورة الحسنة بحسب المعنى والرحمة الإنجاء من كفار مكة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God knows which people He makes manifestations of mercy and which of severity, guiding the former and leading the latter into misguidance and punishment.
rows.anchor: هو أعلم بمن جعله منكم مظهر صفة لطفه ورحمته فيرحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent as bearer of good news and warning, not to compel faith; believers should use patience and gentle forbearance, as God commanded him to show people cordiality alongside fulfilling obligations.
rows.anchor: موكولا إليك يا محمد أمورهم ومفوضا تجبرهم على الإيمان

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: He said God commanded him to deal gently with people just as He commanded him to fulfill the obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: إن الله أمرني بمداراة الناس كما أمرني بإقامة الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people's inward and outward states and selects those worthy of prophethood and sainthood, rebutting Quraysh's objection to an orphan Prophet and poor followers rather than elite leaders; the sky reference rebuts their demand for angels and the earth reference their demand for a grand man from Mecca or Taif.
rows.anchor: وهو رد لاستبعاد قريش أن يكون يتيم أبي طالب نبيا وأن يكون العراة الجوع أصحابه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the heavens, angels and Iblis manifest mercy and severity; on earth, believers and unbelievers manifest those attributes.
rows.anchor: مظهر صفة لطفه ومن جعل منهم مظهر صفة قهره في السموات كالملائكة وإبليس

rows.speaker: البيضاوي وأبو السعود
rows.claim: They say prophetic precedence lies in spiritual virtues and freedom from bodily attachments, not wealth or followers; David's honor was revelation rather than kingship.
rows.anchor: بالفضائل النفسانية والتبري من العلائق الجسمانية لا بكثرة الأموال والاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects bodily detachment as the measure among prophets: worldly possessions and their absence are equal for them; their distinctions are scripture, mission, intimacy with God, speech, ascension, vision, intercession, and similar gifts, as the Qur'an explains itself.
rows.anchor: فالوجه أن التفضيل إنما هو بالكتاب والرسالة والخلة والتكليم والمعراج والرؤية والشفاعة

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: He lists distinctive gifts of Solomon, Jesus, Moses, Salih, Hud, Abraham, and Joseph, and says unequal prophetic readiness for divine manifestation produces differences in prophetic rank and provision; as essential saints they are one, so none is superior, consistent with the Prophet's prohibition on preferring him among prophets.
rows.anchor: فضل سليمان عليه السلام بالظهور بمجموع الملك وعيسى بالكلام في المهد والتأييد بروح القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David's Zabur, given as an honor, contained 150 chapters of glorification, praise, and supplication, without legal rulings; its indefinite and definite forms in this and 21:105 refer to the same named book.
rows.anchor: كان زبور داود مائة وخمسين سورة ليس فيها حلال ولا حرام ولا فرائض ولا حدود

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Primordial wisdom raises the accepted and lowers the rejected as manifestations of mercy and severity; prophets differ in nearness and how divine care spreads through their communities, with the Prophet, his community, and Qur'an foremost, just as Qur'an exceeds Zabur.
rows.anchor: فضلنا الأنبياء بعضهم على بعض بارتفاع المكان في القربة وقبول أثر نظر العناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists are told to call on their alleged deities, including angels, Christ, Mary, and Ezra, but these beings cannot remove or transfer affliction such as illness, poverty, or drought.
rows.anchor: إزالة نحو المرض والفقر والقحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those called upon seek nearness to their own Lord through obedience and worship; even the nearest seek a means to Him, so lesser beings cannot be gods, and all hope for mercy and fear punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني تقرب ميكنند بطاعت وعبادت او بحضرت

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: He offers an interrogative parsing: the worshippers seek which of their gods is nearest to God so they can use that one as intermediary.
rows.anchor: أو أيهم استفهام مبتدأ خبره أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment deserves fear even from prophets and angels; sinners who fail to fear expose their heedlessness, so people should beware the Almighty's force.
rows.anchor: حقيقيا بأن يحذره كل أحد حتى الرسل والملائكة وإن لم يحذره العصاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Umar was stabbed, Ibn Abbas praised his early faith, jihad, the Prophet's approval, and martyrdom; Umar replied that only the deluded are deluded by such praise and said he would ransom himself from the terrors beyond death with all the sun shines upon.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال لعمر رضي الله عنه حين طعن

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: He limits the town to an unbelieving town and says it must be destroyed before Resurrection or its people severely punished through worldly calamities or afterlife punishment; only destruction is explicitly time-limited in his reading.
rows.anchor: المراد بها القرية الكافرة أي : ما من قرية الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects that broad reading as unsuited to context: “before Resurrection” applies to punishment too; destruction means total ruin, while chastisement means afflictions worse than death, without denying later punishment.
rows.anchor: هذا التعميم لا يناسب سوق الآية وقيد القبلية معتبر في الشق الثاني أيضا

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He understands town universally and cites reports that this community's worldly share of punishment is killing, earthquakes, and strife, and its share of hell is calamity beneath the earth; a saying distinguishes ruin for good towns from chastisement for wicked ones.
rows.anchor: إن أمتي أمة مرحومة إنما جعل عذابها في القتل والزلازل والفتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Traditional forecasts assign different destructions to towns: Mecca to Abyssinians, Medina to famine, Basra to flood, Aila to Iraqis, Syria to Romans, Egypt to the Nile's failure, and other regions to named peoples or disasters.
rows.anchor: خراب مكة من الحبشة وخراب المدينة من الجوع وخراب البصرة من الغرق

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: He reports a sequence in which Jazira is safe until Armenia falls, Armenia until Egypt, Egypt until Kufa; the great battle follows Kufa's ruin, and Constantinople is conquered by a man of Hashim's family.
rows.anchor: وروي عن وهب بن منبه أن الجزيرة آمنة من الخراب حتى تخرب أرمينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town's destruction or chastisement, its causes, and its appointed time are written in the Preserved Tablet; two reports describe the pen writing all events through Resurrection and then being sealed.
rows.anchor: مكتوبا لم يغادر منه شيء إلا بين فيه كيفياته وأسبابه الموجبة له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report says God first created the Pen and then the inkwell, ordered it to write all past and future events, and sealed it until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: رواه ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Esoterically, a town is the human body: God destroys its heart and spirit before bodily death, or afflicts it with trials, illness, loss, discipline, and struggle against desire; separation from familiar things is severe and predestined.
rows.anchor: بصب البلاء والمحن والأمراض والعلل والمصائب والنقص في الأموال والأنفس

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The sincere traveler reaches the divine presence only by crossing a steep obstacle and enduring hardship; the stages are dissolution of acts, then attributes, then self, and no prophet suffered as Muhammad did.
rows.anchor: فلا يصل السائر الصادق المحب إلى سرادقات جلاله شوقا إلى جماله إلا بعد العبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs Quraysh proposed included raising the dead, turning Mount al-Safa into gold, removing Mecca's mountains to create arable flat land, and making rivers flow to produce gardens.
rows.anchor: إحياء الموتى وقلب الصفا ذهبا ورفع جبال مكة لتنبسط الأرض وتصلح للزراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing but the earlier peoples' denial kept God from sending the requested signs: people like Aad and Thamud would deny them and merit annihilation, but God has decreed not to eradicate Quraysh because future believers may arise among them or their descendants.
rows.anchor: إلا تكذيب الأولين الذين هم أمثالهم في الطبع كعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel was granted at Thamud's request as a clear sign; “mubsira” marks its evident, sight-worthy character, with the observer's state attributed to it figuratively.
rows.anchor: بينة ذات أبصار على أن يكون للنسبة فالتاء للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud did more than disbelieve: they hamstrung the camel and thereby wronged themselves, bringing destruction; it is singled out because they were Arabs familiar with the ruins.
rows.anchor: لم يكتفوا بمجرد الكفر بها بل فعلوا بها ما فعلوا من العقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requested signs warn like an advance guard of annihilating punishment; alternatively, ordinary miracles and Qur'anic signs warn of afterlife punishment, deferred to Judgment in honor of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: من نزول العذاب المستأصل كالطليعة له فإن لم يخافوا نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report calls the Prophet the greatest protection while he lives and his Sunna endures, but says divine punishment comes if it is extinguished; this community receives some worldly chastisement late in time, including quakes, fears, plague, and tyrants.
rows.anchor: إن الرسول عليه السلام هو الأمان الأعظم ما عاش وما دامت سنته باقية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: He said whoever revives his Sunna has revived him, and whoever loves him will be with him in Paradise.
rows.anchor: من أحيا سنتي فقد أحياني ومن أحياني فقد أحبني ومن أحبني كان معي في الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A second report promises four gifts to one who preserves the Sunna: love among the righteous, awe among the wicked, ample provision, and confidence in religion; the Prophet's perfect heir likewise protects those who believe in and follow his way.
rows.anchor: من حفظ سنتي أكرمه الله بأربع خصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's encompassing means He knows and controls people, who remain in His grasp; the Prophet should carry out his mission without fear.
rows.anchor: علما وقدرة فهم في قبضته فامض لأمرك ولا تخف أحدا

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: For gnostics, God's encompassing is His manifestation through all forms: His names pervade beings as essence, life, knowledge, and power; no atom escapes, and this is neither containment nor a whole-part relation but the relation of an absolute ground to its determinations without compromising unity.
rows.anchor: إحاطة الله سبحانه عند العارفين بالموجودات كلها عبارة عن تجليه بصور الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision was the Prophet's eyewitnessing of wonders of earth and heaven on the Night Journey; “vision” may mean sight while awake, a fleeting nighttime experience, the opponents' claimed dream, or a metaphor for its extraordinary quality.
rows.anchor: المراد بالرؤيا ما عاينه عليه السلام ليلة المعراج من عجائب الأرض والسماء

rows.speaker: الحواشي السعدية
rows.claim: He suggests calling it a vision by metaphor because its marvels transcend ordinary experience and resemble dreams.
rows.anchor: تسميتها رؤيا على وجه التشبيه والاستعارة لما فيها من الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The actual sight of the Night Journey was a tremendous sign, yet became a trial when people denied it and some apostatized.
rows.anchor: وما جعلنا الرؤية التي أريناكها ليلة الإسراء عيانا مع كونها آية عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accursed tree is Zaqqūm, whose eaters are named by metonymy or which is far from mercy; it tested them because they denied a tree could grow in Hell and burn stone, despite familiar fire-resistant or fire-eating examples.
rows.anchor: تلك الشجرة التي هي الزقوم تنبت في أصل الجحيم في أبعد مكان من الرحمة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: He mocks their inconsistency: they draw fire from green trees, as Yā Sīn 36:80 says, yet fail to consider that God can place fire in a tree and grow a tree in fire; rubbing the green male and female morakh and afar branches produces sparks.
rows.anchor: وهي فكر نمى كردندكه آتش در درخت وديعت نهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings only increase the deniers' excessive rebellion; proposed miracles would likewise be rejected and bring the fate of earlier peoples, while general punishment is deferred until the final catastrophe.
rows.anchor: فلو أنا أرسلنا بما اقترحوه من الآيات لفعلوا بها ما فعلوا

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: God told Jesus that many handsome, eloquent, healthy people will cry out amid the layers of Hellfire, so everyone must fear; even gnostics fear, all the more so others.
rows.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى عيسى عليه السلام كم من وجه مليح صبيح ولسان فصيح

rows.speaker: المزني
rows.claim: Visiting al-Shafiʿi in his fatal illness, he heard him say he was leaving the world, meeting his deeds, and could not tell whether his soul would go to Paradise or Fire; the author adds a verse about not knowing which fate will come or when death arrives.
rows.anchor: دخلت على الشافعي رحمه الله في مرضه الذي مات فيه فقلت له : كيف أصبحت

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: Fear is the proper provision for those who are afraid: reassuring the fearful steadies them, while the fearless need no lesson in fear.
rows.anchor: لا تخافوا هست نزل خائفان هست درخور از براى خائفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs and their hearing increase believers' faith and certainty; receptive hearts are like good soil nourished by pure water, while unprepared hearts yield nothing.
rows.anchor: رؤية الآيات واستماعها تزيد المؤمنين إيمانا وتقويهم في باب اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate addresses the angels other than the exalted spirits wholly absorbed in divine witnessing, who were unaware of Adam; the bow was honor for Adam's virtues.
rows.anchor: ما عدا الأرواح العالية وهم الملائكة المهيمة الذين لا شعور لهم بخلق آدم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God manifested Himself in Adam, so the prostration was truly to God, with Adam serving as the qibla like the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: أن الله خلق آدم فتجلى فيه فكانت السجدة في الحقيقة للحق تعالى وكان آدم بمثابة الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels obeyed promptly; their obedience signifies primordial felicity, while Iblis's defiance and pride disclose primordial misery, as the end mirrors the beginning.
rows.anchor: فدل ائتمارهم بأوامر الحق والانتهاء عن نواهيه على السعادة الأزلية

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He says Iblis was a jinn, but is excepted from the angels as a connected exception because he was commanded along with them; he explains the form by masculine grammatical dominance.
rows.anchor: استثنى إبليس من الملائكة وهو جني لأنه قد أمر بالسجود معهم فغلبوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When rebuked, Iblis arrogantly treated the command as an impossible indignity, claiming fire was superior to clay; “shall I prostrate?” is a denial, and “clay” follows an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: وأنا مخلوق من العنصر العالي وهو النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis speaks from enmity and envy after his curse; the reported speech is not immediately after his previous words but after God granted the respite he requested.
rows.anchor: إظهارا للعداوة وإقداما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “Have You considered this one,” the attached kāf is an emphatic address particle, not an object; the first object is “this,” while the second is omitted, and the idiom means “tell me.”
rows.anchor: بل هو حرف أكد به ضمير الفاعل المخاطب لتأكيد الإسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis asks why Adam was honored with vicegerency and the angels' prostration when Iblis believes fire makes him better than clay; the Mathnawi contrasts seeing only Adam's body with seeing his trusted light.
rows.anchor: لم كرمته علي وفضلته بالخلافة والسجود وأنا خير منه لأنه خلق من طين وخلقت من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Iblis is kept alive until Resurrection, he vows to overpower Adam's descendants through seduction, as supported by his oath in Ṣād 38:82.
rows.anchor: لاستولين على أولاده ونسله استيلاء قويا بالإغواء

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The threat can mean either strongly leading the descendants astray with a bridle, or stripping them away through seduction as locusts strip a land.
rows.anchor: من قولهم حنكت الدابة واحتنكتها إذا جعلت في حنكها الأسفل حبلا تقودها به

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Iblis knew that innate desires would turn Adam's descendants from truth to falsehood, by analogy with their father being drawn to eat the tree through desire.
rows.anchor: علم إبليس أن فيهم شهوات مركبة فهي سبب ميلهم عن الحق إلى الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few descendants escape his seduction: those God protects as sincere servants.
rows.anchor: وهم المخلصون الذين عصمهم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: “Go” means proceed with your intended evil, or it is banishment, abandonment to one's choice, or an expression of contempt and threat rather than literal movement opposite to coming.
rows.anchor: بل معناه امض لما قصدته أو طرد له وتخلية بينه وبين ما سولت له نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow Iblis are those who follow him in misguidance; Hell is the complete recompense for him and them, with the singular addressee expanded to his followers.
rows.anchor: أي : جزاؤك وجزاؤهم فغلب المخاطب رعاية لحق المتبوعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is to unsettle and mislead whoever among Adam's descendants he can; the verb means making light or moving someone from a place.
rows.anchor: أي : استخف وحرك ومنه استفزه الغضب استخفه والاستفزاز

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He glosses the command as leading astray and stirring people up.
rows.anchor: واستزل وحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's voice is his whispering and invitation to evil; anyone who calls to disobedience belongs to his faction and army.
rows.anchor: كل داع إلى معصية الله فهو من حزب إبليس وجنده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Zahidi transmits from him that any utterance not pleasing to God is the voice of Satan.
rows.anchor: ازابن عباس نقل ميكندكه هر آوازى كه نه در رضاى خداى تعالى ازدهان بيرون آيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets Satan's voice as singing and musical instruments, making singers and players his troops; a report threatens the player and a hadith says the Prophet was sent to break instruments and kill pigs.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد بالغناء والمزامير فالمغنون والزامرون من جند إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruments named may represent all musical instruments by common usage; “breaking” is emphatic prohibition rather than literal breaking, while David's “psalms” praise describes the sweetness of a Qur'an reciter's voice, not approval of instruments.
rows.anchor: ضرب المزامير مثلا لحسن صوت داود عليه السلام وحلاوة نغمته

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Esoterically, Satan's voice includes deceptive philosophical claims, sectarian analogies, atheist fables, libertine excess, and naturalist doctrines contrary to religious law.
rows.anchor: بتمويهات الفلاسفة وتشبيهات أهل الأهواء والبدع وخرافات الدهرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling out with cavalry and foot soldiers means rallying corrupt helpers, riders, walkers, and demonic auxiliaries against people; al-Kawashi glosses the verb as urging and shouting, citing “O God's cavalry, ride.”
rows.anchor: صح عليهم بأعوانك وأنصارك من راكب وراجل من أهل الفساد
